title.full: ASEAN Green Future Project Phase 2.2 Report, Optimization of Laos's Power Generation Sector

publisher.full: Sustainable Development Solutions Network and ClimateWorks Centre

description: Policy-supported coal phaseout and renewables deployment significantly reduce emissions by 2050.

coreDrivers.policies: Hydro additions are aligned with the NDC until 2030 and continue until the maximum hydro potential in Lao. As coal power is phased out in 2040 and needs to be replaced, additional wind and solar are added to the pathway.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: Near-zero 2050 and coal phase-out by 2040 constrain the pathway.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: SSP2 GDP, medium population growth extracted from World Bank and some ambitous electrification assumptions in housings and transportation drive electricity demand.

dependencies.dependency_description: MAP deals with the policy dependency by imposing a more ambitious renewable build-out and a stated coal phase-out by 2040. These assumptions drive the shift toward near-zero power emissions.
The scenario provider suggests that the pathway would be more easily achievable with: supportive rules for clean-energy investment and regional trading cooperation.

MAP prioritizes the more ambitious decarbonization assumptions and requires substantial clean-power investment; economics is therefore accommodated through higher investment rather than used to determine the technology mix through least-cost optimization. Cross-border electricity trade with Thailand is economically important, but the pathway does not provide forward-looking trade volumes or prices that determine the MAP outcome.

MAP deals with demand-side behavior through much stronger exogenous electrification assumptions, including 50% passenger EV penetration in 2030 and 100% in 2050 and substantially higher electric-truck uptake. This raises electricity demand, but consumer preferences itself is not modeled endogenously.

MAP combines the full hydro build-out with much larger wind and solar capacity, increasing the importance of system integration, but the pathway does not quantify the grid infrastructure required to enable that mix.

Hydropower maxiumum potential ressources is reached by 2050 and is the limit to hydro expansion in Lao. Hydro is then seconded by additional wind and solar capacity to reach near-zero emissions power in Lao.

Seasonal water availability affects hydropower adequacy in the dry season. Laos power grid is already dependant on Thailand during that period. MAP does not introduce a future change in hydrology or an environmental constraint on hydro deployment. MAP therefore proceeds using the stated hydro potential without modelling future ecosystem/climate impacts.
The electrical system requires substantial human resources for its operation. This is not measured in this analysis.
